title: Introduce cost-fusion agent and quant annealer for tenant-specific defaults
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Adds a Cost-Fusion Agent service that synthesizes tenant workload signals to auto-propose batching, cache-warmup and quantization defaults; includes a small annealer process to refine quant profiles with safety fallbacks. No breaking changes to public API.
commits: a1b2c3: introduce cost-fusion agent scaffold and RPC contracts
d4e5f6: implement lightweight tenant simulator and unit-econ scorer
a7b8c9: quant annealer core + safe-fallbacks and profile repo integration
0f1e2d: hotfix config defaults and env var toggles for private deployments
9c8b7a: add e2e smoke tests and CI matrix for quant/tenant permutations
body:
Context and motivation: We frequently see tenants that could benefit from a coordinated set of defaults across batching, cache warmup, and quantization profiles. Individually tuning each knob is error-prone and expensive; operators often pick conservative defaults to avoid regressions which increases unit cost. This PR introduces the Cost-Fusion Agent: a lightweight service that aggregates short-term workload signals and historical unit-econ estimates to propose tenant-specific defaults and an accompanying Quant Annealer that tests gentle quant steps in a safety-first way. The goal is to push reasonable cost wins with minimal manual intervention while preserving quality and latency SLOs.

What this change does (high level): Adds a new service (cost-fusion-agent) and an optional background job (quant-annealer) that work together to generate and validate default configurations per tenant. The agent observes request size distribution, tail latency, hot KV cache hit rates, and historical model accuracy deltas (from eval sets) to synthesize a recommended triplet: batch_size_default, cache_warmup_policy, quant_profile_candidate. The annealer materializes short, controlled validation runs against a shadow queue of traffic or replay samples and records unit-econ delta and quality checks. If the candidate passes safety gates, the recommendation is written into the tenant defaults store as a suggested profile, and surfaced in Console and CLI as a non-destructive suggestion.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: All behavior is behind the feature-flag COST_FUSION_AGENT enabled per-tenant. Defaults remain unchanged for tenants who do not opt-in. For Private deployments we add an env toggle (ENABLE_QUANT_ANNEALER=false) to avoid running anneals in air-gapped installations. No runtime interface changes to external APIs.

Design notes and safety: The annealer uses conservative quant steps (e.g., float32->int8 via calibrated PTQ path with KV-cache compatibility checks) and never auto-promotes a profile without explicit approval or a positive safe-window (observed for N consecutive anneals and unit-econ improvement above threshold). Quality gates include prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE or internal similarity scores, latency and p99 tail overhead, and a rollback timer. The agent exposes a dry-run mode in the Console for operators to preview expected cost delta.

Migration and deployment plan: 1) Deploy cost-fusion-agent as a new deployment in the host cluster (small resource footprint); 2) Enable feature-flag for internal dogfood tenants; 3) Run annealer in dry-run mode for two weeks and review suggestions dashboard; 4) Gradually roll to more tenants with manual approvals. For Dedicated customers we will enable the agent as an opt-in addon in the console.

Testing and observability: Added metrics: fusion.agent.suggestions.count, fusion.agent.approved.count, annealer.run.duration_ms, annealer.quality.failures, annealer.unit_econ.delta. New Console panels: tenant-suggested-profiles and quant-anneal-history. E2E tests include simulated tenant traces with controlled latencies and a replay harness that checks the annealer's quality gates. CI: matrix runs across small/medium/large sample sizes.

Files changed (summary):
- services/cost-fusion-agent/{main.go,agent.go,simulator.go,proto/api.proto}  -- new service and core logic
- services/quant-annealer/{annealer.go,runner.go,profiles.go} -- annealing/validation logic and safe-fallbacks
- pkg/tenants/defaults_store.go -- add write/read API for suggested profiles with metadata and audit fields
- console/components/tenant-suggestions.tsx -- UI for previewing suggested defaults
- test/replay/fixtures/{small,medium}/ -- new fixtures for annealer e2e
- ci/workflows/annealer-matrix.yml -- adds an annealer job matrix for CI
- docs/ops/cost-fusion-agent.md -- operational runbook and toggles

Small illustrative snippet (agent rule matcher):
- services/cost-fusion-agent/agent.go +37 @@
   func scoreSample(s Sample) float64 {
     // estimate token-weighted cost impact and quality delta
     costDelta := estimateCostDelta(s)
     qualityRisk := estimateQualityRisk(s)
     return costDelta / (1.0 + qualityRisk)
   }

Review conversation (selected):
- Mai Tran (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end, biggest question is annealer safety. Please ensure the annealer cannot ship promoted profiles without a manual approval toggle for tenants with >500k monthly tokens."
- Author (Aisha): "Added manual-approval toggle per tenant (defaults_store supports approval flags). For tenants >500k tokens the annealer will only propose suggestions to Console, not auto-apply. Documented in ops runbook."
- Lucas Rivera (reviewer): "Two nits: 1) move the feature flag to runtime flags package, 2) add a short-circuit to skip annealer when replay sample quality is stale."
- Author: "Addressed both in latest commit; moved flag and added freshness check with TTL on replay samples (configurable)."
- Jonah Brooks (reviewer): "CI flaked once on quantized runner on aarch tests, looks resolved after the runner isolation fix."
- Jonah Brooks (approval): "LGTM after CI green and docs added."

CI summary: Initial CI run failed on one aarch quant integration (flake). Reran matrix with isolated runner image; all checks passed. New workflow annealer-matrix runs: linux/amd64, linux/aarch64, small/medium/large fixtures. Unit, integration and e2e smoke tests passed.

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main. Post-merge actions: created console ticket to add a Dashboard card (PM-198) and ops pager recipe for annealer failures. Added a follow-up ticket to extend tenant sampling heuristics (ENG-7301).

Notes and rationale: We purposely keep the initial annealer conservative and visible in Console to build operator trust. The fusion approach reduces repeated manual tuning and captures cross-lever interactions (e.g., a larger batch size may increase cache contention; the agent accounts for that). This PR is intentionally large but modular: agent and annealer live in separate services, defaults_store change is minimal, and UI surfaces are lightweight.

If you'd like to run this locally: see docs/ops/cost-fusion-agent.md for quickstart (docker-compose override that boots agent + annealer local harness).
